methods.label: Compare distances traveled in the same time
methods.explanation:
When First finishes the ten miles, Second has run \(10-2=8\) miles and Third has run \(10-4=6\) miles. These distances were traveled in the same time, so Third's speed is \(\frac68=\frac34\) of Second's speed.

Because both speeds remain constant, Third always travels \(\frac34\) as far as Second in the same elapsed time. When Second reaches ten miles, Third has therefore run
\[
10\cdot\frac34=7\frac12\text{ miles}.
\]
Thus Second beats Third by \(10-7\frac12=2\frac12\) miles, choice C.
methods.levelReason: Uses only constant-speed distance relationships, direct proportion, and fraction arithmetic.
